name: Phenol / Baker-Gordon peel

lead: The Baker-Gordon peel is a deep chemical peel based on phenol and croton oil, introduced in the early 1960s. It is used for deep wrinkles, sun damage and some scarring, and is regarded in the medical literature as the strongest of the traditional peels.

Phenol destroys the outer skin layers and croton oil is described as increasing penetration. The skin then regenerates over days to weeks with new collagen, giving fewer wrinkles and smoother texture. Phenol-croton oil peels were used discreetly by early Hollywood stars in the 1920s and entered mainstream practice in the 1960s. No clinical trials were located; the information comes from encyclopedic summaries.

paras: It is performed under medical supervision with sedation or anaesthesia and cardiac monitoring, usually as a single treatment per area, followed by a long recovery. In looksmaxxing discussions it is a rare, high-stakes procedure.

Reported risks include heart rhythm disturbances from systemic phenol absorption, permanent lightening of skin (hypopigmentation), scarring, infection and herpes reactivation. Wikipedia notes that the deeper the peel, the more complications can arise.

angle.text: The phenol or Baker-Gordon peel is the deepest classic chemical peel, causing a controlled deep injury so skin regenerates with new collagen, for fewer wrinkles and smoother texture. It is performed under medical supervision, and its results are documented mainly in older clinical reports.

lead: The phenol or Baker-Gordon peel is a deep chemical peel in which a mixture containing phenol and croton oil is applied to the skin to produce a controlled deep injury, after which the skin regenerates. It is used for coarse wrinkling, sun-damaged skin and some scarring, and sits at the deepest end of chemical peeling [1][2].

Chemical peeling goes back to the second half of the nineteenth century, when Austrian dermatologist Ferdinand von Hebra used phenol, croton oil and nitric acid for freckles and skin irregularities. Wikipedia states that phenol-croton oil peels were used discreetly by early Hollywood stars in the 1920s and entered mainstream practice in the 1960s through Thomas Baker and Howard Gordon [1]. Grokipedia, an AI-generated source, gives 1961 for the Baker-Gordon formula [2].

Both sources describe the peel as carrying more risk than lighter peels, including cardiac and pigmentation effects [1][2]. No clinical trials were located for this article; the information here comes from encyclopedic summaries, which themselves note limited sourcing.

paras: Wikipedia credits von Hebra (1816-1880) with introducing chemical peeling in the later nineteenth century using phenol, croton oil and nitric acid, and says the phenol-croton oil peel was used clandestinely by Hollywood stars in the 1920s before Thomas Baker and Howard Gordon brought it into mainstream practice in the 1960s [1].

Grokipedia attributes the introduction of phenol as a peeling agent to William Tilbury Fox in 1871 and a description of its peeling properties to Paul Unna in 1882, and dates the Baker-Gordon formula to 1961 (88% phenol with croton oil, hexachlorophene soap and water). It is AI-generated and may contain errors, and Wikipedia is preferred where they differ [2].

Wikipedia classifies phenol-croton oil as the deep peel and notes that early phenol peels were often performed under general anaesthesia, with newer formulations able to use sedation with local anaesthetic [1]. Grokipedia describes the Baker-Gordon formula as a benchmark for profound resurfacing because of its consistent depth [2].
Wikipedia states that complications rise with peel depth and lists prolonged redness, pigment change, skin atrophy, texture change and scarring among them [1].

Grokipedia reports that systemic phenol absorption can cause arrhythmias and cardiotoxicity, especially with pre-existing heart disease or large treated areas, and that laryngeal spasm and renal and pulmonary toxicity have been described. It describes frequent and possibly permanent hypopigmentation, particularly in lighter skin, a higher scarring potential that leads to the peel generally being limited to once per area, and infection and herpes reactivation. It lists pre-procedure ECG and organ function tests, cardiac monitoring, intravenous fluids and application in timed segments as described precautions [2]. These details come from an AI-generated page whose citations are not all clearly matched to its claims.
The peel is categorised on the wiki under hardmaxx as an invasive resurfacing procedure with a reputation for severe downsides. No community threads are cited in this article.
